profile.subseg: Antique Gold Jewellery; Diamond & Polki Premium Collections; 18K/14K Capsule Lines
profile.themes: Premiumization; Volume-Led Growth; Gold Price Hedging; Regional Design Localization

deepdive.sec: Jewellery / Premium Design-Led Manufacturing & Retail Supply Chain

bull_bear.body: Reinvesting in design R&D (17,000+ designs), regional collection development, and capacity scaling; No dividend or buyback mentioned; Focus on working capital efficiency (targeting 45-day cycle for premium collections)
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Gold price volatility (mitigated by 100% hedging); Over-reliance on retail chain demand; Slow adoption of lower carat jewellery; Aneya brand scaling risk; Competition from casting-focused players with higher volume turnover
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and strategic; focused on volume over revenue due to gold price distortion; clear shift from inventory-led to bulk-order-led model; strong emphasis on design ecosystem and client-specific teams; cautious on FY27 guidance but optimistic on structural growth
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The company is transitioning from a traditional gold jeweller to a B2B design-and-manufacture partner for national chains — clients now supply gold for bulk orders, reducing Ashapuri’s working capital burden and shifting risk to retailers
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Antique gold: 95% of revenue; Diamond/Polki (Aneya): <5% revenue; 18K/14K capsule lines: emerging; Big-box (single-store): 30-40% revenue; Corporate/national chains: 60-65% revenue
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gold price surge erodes volume growth visibility | Ashapuri Gold Ornament Limited | beneficiary | High | 100% gold hedging and bulk-order model insulate margins and working capital, turning price volatility into a structural advantage |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin expanded to 11% (from 5.6% in Q1) due to: (1) 20% volume growth enabling operating leverage; (2) premium studded collections (diamond/polki) driving higher ASP; (3) 100% gold hedging eliminating input volatility; (4) design-led innovation reducing waste and improving yield
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue growth: 18-25% FY26 (down from initial 45-50% due to gold price surge); Margin: Stable with upward bias via product mix; Order inflow: Expecting further growth from Jan 2026 IIJS; Capex/commissioning: 1.5 ton annual capacity (current 750kg); expansion possible to 1 ton with 40-60 day lead time
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: INR107.41cr total (INR102cr from IIJS 2025 + INR5.41cr Aneya diamond/polki); Two national chains in final negotiation; Jan 2026 IIJS expected to add further orders
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Expansion into lower carat (18K/14K) jewellery; Regional capsule collections (West India); Bulk order model with client-supplied gold; Aneya premium line scaling; Potential export via design licensing
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Ashapuri delivered strong Q2FY26 volume growth (20% YoY) and EBITDA margin expansion to 11% due to premium product mix and 100% gold hedging, with order book surging to INR107.41cr; the company is shifting from inventory-led to bulk-order-led growth, enhancing margin resilience despite gold price volatility.

meta.thesis: Ashapuri delivered strong Q2FY26 volume growth (20% YoY) and EBITDA margin expansion to 11% due to premium product mix and 100% gold hedging, with order book surging to INR107.41cr; the company is shifting from inventory-led to bulk-order-led growth, enhancing margin resilience despite gold price volatility.
